subject: mathematics
stem: The general solution of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}=x^3\cos^2y-x\sin2y$ is
explanation: Divide by $\cos^2y$: $\sec^2y\,y'+2x\tan y=x^3$. With $u=\tan y$: $u'+2xu=x^3$, IF $e^{x^2}$. $ue^{x^2}=\int x^3e^{x^2}dx=\frac12(x^2-1)e^{x^2}+C$, so $\tan y=\frac12(x^2-1)+Ce^{-x^2}$. Option (1) has no arbitrary constant; (3),(4) use the wrong integrating-factor sign.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q80)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A motorist completes half revolution on a circular path of $60\ \mathrm{m}$ radius in one minute. His average speed
explanation: Distance for half a revolution $=\pi r=60\pi\approx188.4$ m in 60 s, so average speed $=\pi\approx3.14\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. $2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ is the average velocity (displacement $2r=120$ m over 60 s), a common confusion of speed with velocity.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q82)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: If the vertical displacement of a body projected at an angle with the horizontal during the first second of its motion is $15\ \mathrm{m}$, then the maximum height reached by it is (acceleration due to gravity $=10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$)
explanation: $y=u_y t-\tfrac12 gt^2$: $15=u_y(1)-5\Rightarrow u_y=20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. $H=u_y^2/2g=400/20=20$ m. Using $u_y^2/g$ (40 m) or ignoring gravity in the first second gives wrong options.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q83)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: If the resultant of three vectors $\vec A=-\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k$, $\vec B=-2\hat i-\hat j-4\hat k$ and $\vec C$ is a vector in the positive $z$-direction with a magnitude of 2 units, then the vector $\vec C=$
explanation: $\vec A+\vec B=-3\hat i+\hat j-\hat k$. Resultant $=2\hat k$, so $\vec C=2\hat k-(-3\hat i+\hat j-\hat k)=3\hat i-\hat j+3\hat k$. Sign slips when subtracting $\vec A+\vec B$ lead to the other options.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q84)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A block of mass $2\ \mathrm{kg}$ placed on a rough horizontal surface is pulled with a force of $30\ \mathrm{N}$ which makes an angle of $\sin^{-1}(0.6)$ with the horizontal. If the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the surface is 0.4, then the acceleration of the block is (Acceleration due to gravity $=10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$)
explanation: Horizontal component $30(0.8)=24$ N; vertical component $30(0.6)=18$ N upward, so $N=20-18=2$ N and friction $=0.4\times2=0.8$ N. $a=(24-0.8)/2=11.6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Taking $N=mg=20$ N (friction 8 N) is the common trap.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q85)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A body of mass $5\ \mathrm{kg}$ at rest is acted upon by two forces $30\ \mathrm{N}$ and $F$. If the angle between the forces is $60^\circ$ and the distance travelled by the body in a time of $2\ \mathrm{s}$ under the action of these forces is $28\ \mathrm{m}$, then $F=$
explanation: $s=\tfrac12at^2\Rightarrow28=2a\Rightarrow a=14$, so resultant $R=70$ N. $R^2=30^2+F^2+2(30)F\cos60^\circ$: $F^2+30F-4000=0\Rightarrow F=50$ N. Adding the forces linearly ($F=40$ N) ignores the angle.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q86)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: If the ratio of the potential and kinetic energies of a body of mass $3\ \mathrm{kg}$ thrown vertically upwards at a height of $40\ \mathrm{m}$ is $2:3$, then the kinetic energy of the body at a height of $65\ \mathrm{m}$ is (Acceleration due to gravity $=10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$)
explanation: At 40 m, $PE=3\times10\times40=1200$ J, so $KE=1800$ J and total energy $=3000$ J. At 65 m, $PE=1950$ J, so $KE=3000-1950=1050$ J. 1950 J is the PE and 3000 J the total energy - both traps.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q87)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: If the work done in increasing the velocity of a body by 25% is $900\ \mathrm{J}$, then the work done in decreasing the velocity of the same body by 25% is
explanation: Work = change in KE. Increase: $K(1.25^2-1)=0.5625K=900\Rightarrow K=1600$ J. Decrease: $K(1-0.75^2)=0.4375\times1600=700$ J. Assuming the same 900 J or linear scaling ignores that KE goes as $v^2$.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q88)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A torque $T$ produces angular acceleration $\alpha$ in a circular disc. If radius of disc is doubled keeping the mass constant, angular acceleration becomes
explanation: $I=\tfrac12MR^2$; doubling $R$ makes $I$ four times. With the same torque, $\alpha=T/I$ becomes $\alpha/4$. $\alpha/2$ wrongly assumes $I\propto R$; $4\alpha$ inverts the relation.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q89)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: Hollow sphere rolls on an inclined plane of height $h$ without slipping. If it starts from rest, its speed at the bottom is
explanation: $v=\sqrt{\dfrac{2gh}{1+k^2/R^2}}$ with $k^2/R^2=2/3$ for a hollow sphere: $v=\sqrt{6gh/5}$. $\sqrt{10gh/7}$ is for a solid sphere, $\sqrt{4gh/3}$ for a disc/solid cylinder, $\sqrt{2gh}$ for pure sliding.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q90)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: In SHM, velocity leads displacement by
explanation: $x=A\sin\omega t$, $v=A\omega\cos\omega t=A\omega\sin(\omega t+\pi/2)$, so velocity leads displacement by $90^\circ$. $180^\circ$ is the phase lead of acceleration over displacement.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q91)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: For a planet having uniform density, the Gravitational field inside the planet varies with the distance from the centre as
explanation: Inside a uniform sphere only the mass within radius $r$ attracts: $g=GMr/R^3\propto r$. The $1/r^2$ law applies only outside the planet.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q93)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A book of dimension $4\ \mathrm{cm}\times1.5\ \mathrm{cm}\times10\ \mathrm{cm}$ is kept in a way that the $10\ \mathrm{cm}$ edge is vertical. A horizontal force of $3\ \mathrm{N}$ is applied at the top face. If the shear modulus of the book is $2\times10^5\ \mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}$, then the horizontal displacement of the top face will be
explanation: Top face area $=4\times1.5=6\ \mathrm{cm^2}=6\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^2}$. Shear stress $=3/(6\times10^{-4})=5000$ Pa; strain $=5000/(2\times10^5)=0.025$. Displacement $=0.025\times10$ cm $=2.5$ mm. Using a side face as the area gives the wrong options.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q94)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A bubble rises in a viscous liquid. If radius of bubble doubles, terminal velocity becomes
explanation: Terminal velocity $v=\dfrac{2r^2(\rho-\sigma)g}{9\eta}\propto r^2$ (magnitude), so doubling $r$ makes it four times. 'Double' wrongly assumes $v\propto r$.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q95)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: At what temperature, Celsius scale and Fahrenheit scale will coincide
explanation: $F=\tfrac95C+32$; setting $F=C$: $-\tfrac45C=32\Rightarrow C=-40$. So $-40^\circ\mathrm{C}=-40^\circ\mathrm{F}$.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q96)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: When an iron rod is heated, the variation of color from dull red to white can be explained by
explanation: Wien's law $\lambda_mT=b$: as temperature rises the peak wavelength shifts to shorter wavelengths, so colour changes from red towards white. Stefan's law gives total emitted power, not colour; Newton's law concerns cooling rate.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q97)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: Equal amounts of a diatomic ideal gas are contained in two separate cylinders, P and Q. Cylinder P has a movable piston, while cylinder Q has a fixed piston. Both gases are initially at $273\ \mathrm{K}$, and the same amount of heat is supplied to each. If the gas in cylinder P shows a temperature rise of $20\ \mathrm{K}$, then the increase in temperature of the gas in cylinder Q is
explanation: P is at constant pressure, Q at constant volume: $nC_p(20)=nC_v\Delta T_Q\Rightarrow\Delta T_Q=\gamma\times20=1.4\times20=28$ K. Assuming equal rise (20 K) or using a monatomic $\gamma$ are the traps.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q98)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: If the temperature of 3 moles of helium gas is increased by $2\ \mathrm{K}$, then the change in the internal energy of helium gas is
explanation: Helium is monatomic, $C_v=\tfrac32R$. $\Delta U=nC_v\Delta T=3\times\tfrac32\times8.314\times2\approx74.8$ J. Using $C_p$ or a diatomic $C_v$ gives larger values.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q100)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: Two identical strings each of length $0.750\ \mathrm{m}$ are each tuned exactly to $440\ \mathrm{Hz}$. The tension in one of the strings is then increased by $1.0\%$. If they are now struck, then the beat frequency between the fundamentals of the two strings is nearly
explanation: $f\propto\sqrt T$, so $\Delta f/f=\tfrac12(\Delta T/T)=0.5\%$. $\Delta f=0.005\times440=2.2\approx2$ Hz. Taking $f\propto T$ gives 4.4 Hz; the length is irrelevant.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q101)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A convex lens forms a real image and a virtual image of same size of an object placed separately at distances $u_1$ and $u_2$ respectively from the lens. Then the focal length of the lens is
explanation: For equal magnification magnitude $m$: real image $m=\dfrac{f}{u_1-f}$, virtual image $m=\dfrac{f}{f-u_2}$. Equating, $u_1-f=f-u_2\Rightarrow f=\dfrac{u_1+u_2}{2}$. $\sqrt{u_1u_2}$ is a trap borrowed from displacement-method formulas.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q102)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: $n$ transparent films, each of refractive index 1.5 with thickness $1\ \mathrm{cm}, 2\ \mathrm{cm}, 3\ \mathrm{cm},\ldots, n\ \mathrm{cm}$ are placed one over the other. When a point object is seen normally through this combination, the object is found to be shifted by $5\ \mathrm{cm}$. Then the value of $n$ is
explanation: Normal shift $=\sum t\left(1-\tfrac1\mu\right)=\tfrac13\cdot\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}=5\Rightarrow n(n+1)=30\Rightarrow n=5$. Using $1/\mu$ instead of $1-1/\mu$ or ignoring the factor gives wrong values.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q103)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: In Young's double slit experiment, the Y-coordinates of central maxima and $10^{\text{th}}$ maxima are $2\ \mathrm{cm}$ and $5\ \mathrm{cm}$ respectively. When this apparatus is immersed in a liquid of refractive index 1.5, the corresponding Y-coordinates will be
explanation: Central maximum position is unchanged (2 cm). The 10th maximum lies 3 cm from it; this distance scales by $1/\mu$: $3/1.5=2$ cm, so it is at $2+2=4$ cm. Dividing both coordinates by 1.5 (option 4) wrongly shifts the central maximum.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q104)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: Two point charges $-2Q$ and $Q$ are located at $(-3a,0)$ and $(3a,0)$ in the $X$-$Y$ plane. The locus of all points in the $X$-$Y$ plane where electric potential is zero to these charges is
explanation: $V=0\Rightarrow\dfrac{2Q}{r_1}=\dfrac{Q}{r_2}\Rightarrow r_1=2r_2$. The locus of points whose distances from two fixed points are in a constant ratio $\ne1$ is a circle (Apollonius). A straight line (perpendicular bisector) occurs only for equal and opposite charges.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q105)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A particle, having a charge 100 times the charge of an electron, is rotating in a circular path of radius $0.8\ \mathrm{m}$ in 1 second. The value of the magnetic field produced at the centre of the circle will be ($\mu_0$ - permeability of free space)
explanation: Equivalent current $I=qf=100\times1.6\times10^{-19}\times1=1.6\times10^{-17}$ A. $B=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2r}=\dfrac{\mu_0\times1.6\times10^{-17}}{1.6}=10^{-17}\mu_0$. The $10^{-7}$ options confuse the answer with the value of $\mu_0/4\pi$.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q110)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A galvanometer has 30 divisions on its scale. It requires a potential difference of $30\ \mathrm{mV}$ for a current of $1\ \mathrm{mA}$ through its coil, which produces a deflection of one division. The shunt required to convert it into an ammeter of range $0$-$3\ \mathrm{A}$ is
explanation: $G=30\ \mathrm{mV}/1\ \mathrm{mA}=30\ \Omega$; full-scale current $I_g=30\times1\ \mathrm{mA}=0.03$ A. $S=\dfrac{I_gG}{I-I_g}=\dfrac{0.9}{2.97}=\dfrac{10}{33}\ \Omega$. Taking $I_g=1$ mA (one division) gives about $0.01\ \Omega$.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q111)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: If $\chi$ is the magnetic susceptibility, $\mu$, $\mu_0$ and $\mu_r$ are absolute, free space and relative permeabilities respectively, then
explanation: $\mu_r=1+\chi$ and $\mu=\mu_0\mu_r$, so $\mu=\mu_0(1+\chi)$. Option 3 has the wrong sign; options 1 and 4 mix up $\mu_r$ and $\mu_0$.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q112)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A pure inductor of inductance $3\ \mathrm{H}$ (negligible resistance) is connected to a time-varying voltage source such that $v(t)=4t$ volts. Here, $t$ is in seconds. If the voltage is applied at $t=0$, calculate the energy stored in the inductor after $3\ \mathrm{s}$.
explanation: $L\,di/dt=4t\Rightarrow i=\dfrac{2t^2}{3}$; at $t=3$ s, $i=6$ A. $U=\tfrac12Li^2=\tfrac12\times3\times36=54$ J. Using $i=v/L=4$ A at $t=3$ (24 J) skips the integration.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q113)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: To have resonance in a LCR series circuit, the impedance $(Z)$ value
explanation: $Z=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}$; at resonance $X_L=X_C$, so $Z=R$ (minimum). $Z=0$ would hold only for an ideal LC circuit with no resistance; $Z<R$ is impossible.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q114)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: Solar energy flux of $2000\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$ incident normally on a solar plate of $1\ \mathrm{m^2}$ surface area in 1 hour. Then the momentum received by solar plate is
explanation: Energy $U=2000\times1\times3600=7.2\times10^6$ J. For complete absorption $p=U/c=7.2\times10^6/(3\times10^8)=24\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$. $48\times10^{-3}$ assumes perfect reflection ($2U/c$).

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q115)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: When two electrons A and B are accelerated through potential difference $V_A$ and $V_B$ respectively, their de Broglie wave lengths are in the ratio of $2:3$, then the ratio of potential differences $\dfrac{V_A}{V_B}$ is
explanation: $\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}}\propto\dfrac1{\sqrt V}$, so $\dfrac{V_A}{V_B}=\left(\dfrac{\lambda_B}{\lambda_A}\right)^2=\left(\dfrac32\right)^2=9:4$. $4:9$ forgets the inverse relation.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q116)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: In Rutherford $\alpha$ scattering experiment when a particle approaches with an impact parameter zero, its angle of scattering is
explanation: Zero impact parameter means a head-on collision: the $\alpha$ particle stops at the distance of closest approach and retraces its path, so the scattering angle is $\pi$. $0^\circ$ corresponds to a very large impact parameter.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q117)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem:
What is the energy released in the following fission reaction?
${}^{236}_{z}U\rightarrow{}^{117}_{a}X+{}^{117}_{(z-a)}Y+2\left({}^{1}_{0}n\right)$
Given that the binding energy per nucleon of X and Y is $8.8\ \mathrm{MeV}$ and that of ${}^{236}_{z}U$ is $7.5\ \mathrm{MeV}$
explanation: Energy released $=$ BE of products $-$ BE of reactant $=234\times8.8-236\times7.5=2059.2-1770=289.2$ MeV (free neutrons have zero binding energy). Using 236 nucleons for the products ($236\times1.3=306.8$ MeV) is the usual slip.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q118)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: For an amplitude modulated wave, maximum and minimum amplitudes are found to be $12\ \mathrm{V}$ and $4\ \mathrm{V}$. Modulation index is
explanation: $\mu=\dfrac{A_{max}-A_{min}}{A_{max}+A_{min}}=\dfrac{12-4}{12+4}=0.5=50\%$. Taking $(A_{max}-A_{min})/A_{max}$ gives the 67%/75%-type traps.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 12 May Shift 2, Q120)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: The energy of spectral line of lowest frequency in Lyman series of $\mathrm{Li^{2+}}$ spectrum is $x$ J. The energy of second spectral line in Balmer series of $\mathrm{He^{+}}$ spectrum is $y$ J. The ratio of $x$ and $y$ is
explanation: $E\propto Z^2\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2}-\frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$. Li$^{2+}$ Lyman lowest frequency ($2\to1$): $9\times\frac34=\frac{27}{4}$. He$^+$ Balmer second line ($4\to2$): $4\left(\frac14-\frac1{16}\right)=\frac34$. Ratio $x:y=9:1$. Trap: taking the first Balmer line ($3\to2$) or inverting the ratio gives 3:1 or 1:9.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q121)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
Quantum number sets of four electrons I, II, III, IV are given below. The correct order of the energy of these electrons is
I. $n=3, l=1, m_l=-1, m_s=+\frac12$
II. $n=4, l=1, m_l=0, m_s=+\frac12$
III. $n=4, l=2, m_l=-2, m_s=+\frac12$
IV. $n=3, l=2, m_l=-1, m_s=-\frac12$
The correct answer is
explanation: Use the $(n+l)$ rule: I (3p) = 4, II (4p) = 5, III (4d) = 6, IV (3d) = 5. For equal $n+l$, higher $n$ has higher energy, so II (4p) > IV (3d). Order: III > II > IV > I. Trap: missing the tie-break and placing 3d above 4p gives III > IV > II > I.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q122)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: Which of the following statement is not correct?

options.text: The increasing order of first ionization enthalpy of Be, B, C is B < Be < C
The IUPAC name of element Livermorium is ununhexium
The element Tennessene belongs to group 16 in periodic table

explanation: Tennessine (Z = 117) is in group 17 (halogen family), not group 16, so (3) is wrong. (1) is correct: B has lower IE than Be (2p electron easier to remove). (2) Lv, Z = 116, is ununhexium. (4) $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$ and $\mathrm{As_2O_3}$ are both amphoteric.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q123)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: Identify the correct pair of species having same number of valency electrons
explanation: Count total valence electrons: $\mathrm{CCl_4}=4+4(7)=32$; $\mathrm{PO_4^{3-}}=5+24+3=32$ - equal. Others: $\mathrm{SF_4}=34$, $\mathrm{ClO_3^-}=26$, $\mathrm{ClF_3}=28$, $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}=32$. Trap: forgetting to add the ionic charge.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q124)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: Which of the following orders is not correct for the property mentioned against them?

options.text: C$-$C > N$-$O > C$-$O > C$-$H - bond length

explanation: Average bond lengths: C$-$C 154 pm, C$-$O 143 pm, N$-$O 136 pm, C$-$H 107 pm, so N$-$O < C$-$O and order (3) is wrong. (1) b.p. 373 > 293 > 240 > 213 K is correct; (2) dipole 1.85 > 1.47 > 0.23 > 0 D correct; (4) bond orders 2.5 > 2 > 1.5 > 1 correct.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q125)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: At 300 K, air is present in an open round bottom flask of volume 10 L. The flask is heated to 750 K. Some air is expelled from the flask. What is the fraction of air expelled from the flask? (Assume air as an ideal gas)
explanation: Open flask: $P$, $V$ constant, so $nT$ = constant. $n_2/n_1=300/750=2/5$ remains; fraction expelled $=1-\frac25=\frac35$. Trap: $\frac25$ is the fraction remaining, not expelled.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q126)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: White phosphorous reacts with aqueous NaOH solution to form $\mathrm{PH_3(g)}$ and aqueous sodium hypophosphite. 124 g of white phosphorous reacts completely with 1 L of $x$ M NaOH to form three moles of sodium hypophosphite. What is the volume (in L) of $x$ M NaOH that completely reacts with 128 g of rhombic sulphur to form aqueous sulphide, water and aqueous thiosulphate? (P = 31 u; S = 32 u)
explanation: $\mathrm{P_4+3NaOH+3H_2O\to PH_3+3NaH_2PO_2}$: 124 g = 1 mol $\mathrm{P_4}$ uses 3 mol NaOH, so $x=3$ M. $\mathrm{4S+6NaOH\to 2Na_2S+Na_2S_2O_3+3H_2O}$: 128 g S = 4 mol S needs 6 mol NaOH; $V=6/3=2$ L. Trap: treating 124 g as 4 mol P or taking $x=1$ M leads to other options.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q127)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: At T(K), enthalpy of combustion of C(s), $\mathrm{H_2(g)}$ and $\mathrm{CH_4(g)}$ are $-393.5$, $-286$, $-890$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ respectively. What is the enthalpy of formation of methane (in kJ mol$^{-1}$)?
explanation: $\Delta_fH(\mathrm{CH_4})=\Delta_cH(\mathrm C)+2\Delta_cH(\mathrm{H_2})-\Delta_cH(\mathrm{CH_4})=-393.5-572+890=-75.5$ kJ mol$^{-1}$. Trap: using 1 mol of $\mathrm{H_2}$ instead of 2, or reversing the sign of methane combustion.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q128)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: At 300 K, 1 mole of an ideal gas is allowed to expand isothermally and reversibly from a pressure of 20 atm to 2 atm. The work done (in kJ mol$^{-1}$) in the process is ($R = 8.3$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)
explanation: $w=-2.303\,nRT\log\frac{P_1}{P_2}=-2.303\times8.3\times300\times\log10=-5734$ J $=-5.734$ kJ. Expansion: work done by the system is negative (IUPAC sign). Traps: positive sign, or a factor-of-10 slip (57.34).

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q129)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
Observe the following data given below. Which set of buffer solution has highest pH?
(Buffer solution: volume (in mL) of 1 M solution of weak acid; volume (in mL) of 0.1 M sodium salt of weak acid)
I: 4.0; 4.0
II: 4.0; 40.0
III: 40.0; 4.0
IV: 0.1; 10.0
explanation: $\mathrm{pH=p}K_a+\log\frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{acid}]}$; ratio of mmol salt/acid: I $0.4/4=0.1$, II $4/4=1$, III $0.4/40=0.01$, IV $1/0.1=10$. Largest ratio (IV) gives highest pH. Trap: comparing volumes only and ignoring the different concentrations (1 M vs 0.1 M) would wrongly pick II.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q130)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: For the reaction $2HI(g) \rightleftharpoons H_2(g) + I_2(g)$, the correct expression relating the degree of dissociation ($\alpha$) of $HI$ and equilibrium constant $K_p$ is
explanation: From 1 mol HI: HI $1-\alpha$, $\mathrm{H_2}=\mathrm{I_2}=\alpha/2$. $\Delta n=0$, so $K_p=\frac{\alpha^2/4}{(1-\alpha)^2}$, $\sqrt{K_p}=\frac{\alpha}{2(1-\alpha)}$, giving $\alpha=\frac{2\sqrt{K_p}}{1+2\sqrt{K_p}}$. (1) and (2) can exceed 1, impossible for $\alpha$.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q131)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: In gas phase structure of $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$, the dihedral angle is
explanation: $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ has an open-book structure; dihedral angle is 111.5$^\circ$ in the gas phase and 90.2$^\circ$ in the solid phase. Values near 94.8$^\circ$/101.9$^\circ$ are the O$-$O$-$H bond angles (gas/solid). Trap: confusing bond angle with dihedral angle, or picking the solid-phase value.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q132)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: Which one of the carbonates is unstable in air and is kept in $\mathrm{CO_2}$ atmosphere to avoid decomposition?
explanation: Thermal stability of group 2 carbonates increases down the group. Tiny, highly polarising $\mathrm{Be^{2+}}$ makes $\mathrm{BeCO_3}$ so unstable that it is stored under $\mathrm{CO_2}$ to suppress $\mathrm{BeCO_3\to BeO+CO_2}$. Mg, Ca, Ba carbonates are stable in air.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q133)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: Total number of electrons involved in the formation of bridge bonds in the structure of diborane is
explanation: $\mathrm{B_2H_6}$ has two B$-$H$-$B bridges, each a three-centre two-electron (banana) bond: $2\times2=4$ electrons. Trap: counting 2 (one bridge) or 6 (thinking 3 atoms each contribute).

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q134)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
Consider the following statements
Statement - I: Silica in its normal form is almost non-reactive because of very high Si-O bond enthalpy
Statement - II: Silica has no reaction with HF
The correct answer is

options.text: Both the statements I & II are correct.
Statement I is correct but statement - II is NOT correct
Statement I is NOT correct but statement - II is correct
Both the statements I & II are NOT correct

explanation: Silica is inert due to the high Si$-$O bond enthalpy (I true). But it is attacked by HF: $\mathrm{SiO_2+4HF\to SiF_4+2H_2O}$ (used to etch glass), so II is false.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q135)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
Identify the sets which contain greenhouse gases only
I. $\mathrm{CO_2, SO_3, N_2}$
II. $\mathrm{CO_2, CH_4, O_3}$
III. $\mathrm{O_2, NO_2, SO_2}$
IV. $\mathrm{O_3}$, CFCs, $\mathrm{N_2O}$
The correct answer is
explanation: Greenhouse gases include $\mathrm{CO_2, CH_4, O_3, N_2O}$, CFCs and water vapour. Set I has $\mathrm{N_2}$ and set III has $\mathrm{O_2}$, which are not greenhouse gases. So only II and IV.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q136)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: An organic compound containing an extra element $E$ on reaction with $\mathrm{Na_2O_2}$ followed by boiling with $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ gives a compound. This on treatment with ammonium molybdate solution gives yellow precipitate. What is $E$?
explanation: Phosphorus is oxidised by $\mathrm{Na_2O_2}$ to phosphate; with $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ and ammonium molybdate it forms yellow ammonium phosphomolybdate, $\mathrm{(NH_4)_3PO_4\cdot12MoO_3}$. S gives violet with nitroprusside, N gives Prussian blue, and iodine is tested with $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ (yellow AgI), not molybdate.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q137)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
The number of hyperconjugative hydrogens present in the product $Y$ is
$\mathrm{CH_2=CH_2} \xrightarrow{HBr} X \xrightarrow[\text{Anhy. }AlCl_3]{C_6H_6} Y$
explanation: $X$ = $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Br}$; Friedel-Crafts alkylation gives $Y$ = ethylbenzene, $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2CH_3}$. Hyperconjugation with the ring involves only $\alpha$-(benzylic) C$-$H bonds: 2. Trap: counting the 3 methyl H's or all 5 alkyl H's.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q138)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
Which of the following compounds will show geometrical isomerism?
I. $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C=CH\,C_2H_5}$
II. $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH=CH\,C_2H_5}$
III. $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH=CH_2}$
IV. $\mathrm{CH_3CH=C(Cl)CH_3}$
The correct answer is
explanation: Cis-trans isomerism needs two different groups on each double-bond carbon. II (Ph/H and Et/H) and IV ($\mathrm{CH_3}$/H and Cl/$\mathrm{CH_3}$) qualify. I has two $\mathrm{CH_3}$ on one carbon and III has $=\mathrm{CH_2}$, so they cannot.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q139)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: A metal X of atomic mass 75 u forms a cubic lattice of edge length 5 Å. If the density of the lattice is 2 g cm$^{-3}$, the radius (in Å) of the metal atom is ($N = 6\times10^{23}$ mol$^{-1}$)
explanation: $Z=\frac{\rho a^3N}{M}=\frac{2\times125\times10^{-24}\times6\times10^{23}}{75}=2$, so bcc. $r=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}a=\frac{1.732\times5}{4}=2.165$ Å. Trap: 4.330 is $\sqrt3a/2$ (i.e. $2r$); 1.083 is half the radius.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q140)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: An aqueous solution of a non-volatile and non-electrolytic solute boils at 100.5$^\circ$C. What will be the freezing point of the same solution? (Given $K_b = 0.512$ K kg mol$^{-1}$ and $K_f = 1.86$ K kg mol$^{-1}$)
explanation: $m=\Delta T_b/K_b=0.5/0.512=0.977$ mol kg$^{-1}$; $\Delta T_f=K_fm=1.86\times0.977=1.816$ K, so f.p. $=-1.816\,^\circ$C. Traps: $-0.908$ halves and $-3.632$ doubles the depression.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q141)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: X, Y and Z represent three electrodes $\mathrm{Al^{3+}/Al}$, $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}/Cu}$ and $\mathrm{Ag^{+}/Ag}$ with $E^\circ$ values $-1.66$, $0.34$ and $0.80$ V respectively. The correct order of oxidising power of these three electrodes is
explanation: Higher (more positive) standard reduction potential means a stronger oxidising agent: $\mathrm{Ag^+}$ (0.80) > $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ (0.34) > $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ ($-1.66$), i.e. Z > Y > X. X > Y > Z is the order of reducing power.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q142)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: The electrical conductivity of a solution decreases with dilution
Statement II: The overall reaction in $\mathrm{H_2-O_2}$ fuel cell is, $\mathrm{2H_2O(l)\longrightarrow 2H_2(g)+O_2(g)}$
The correct answer is

options.text: Both statements I and statement II are correct
Both statements I and statement II are not correct
Statement I is correct but statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but statement II is correct

explanation: Conductivity ($\kappa$) decreases on dilution as ions per unit volume fall (molar conductivity increases), so I is true. The fuel-cell reaction is $\mathrm{2H_2+O_2\to2H_2O}$; the given equation is electrolysis of water, so II is false.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q143)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: In the Arrhenius equation, $\exp\left(-\frac{E_a}{RT}\right)$, is equal to

options.text: Fraction of molecules that have energy higher than $E_a$

explanation: In $k=Ae^{-E_a/RT}$, the Boltzmann factor $e^{-E_a/RT}$ is the fraction of molecules with energy $\ge E_a$. $A$ is the frequency factor and the product $Ae^{-E_a/RT}$ is the rate constant, not the exponential alone.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q144)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: At T(K), adsorption of acetic acid on 1g of charcoal gave a Freundlich adsorption isotherm with slope of 0.5 and intercept of 1. What is the value of $x$, when the concentration of acetic acid is 0.1 mol L$^{-1}$? (antilog (0.5) = 3.162; antilog (0.301) = 2.0)
explanation: $\log\frac{x}{m}=\log k+\frac1n\log C=1+0.5\log0.1=1-0.5=0.5$. So $x/m=3.162$; with $m=1$ g, $x=3.162$. Trap: dropping the intercept gives 0.3162.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q145)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
Match List - I with List - II
List - I (colloid): A. Smoke; B. Silver sol; C. Antimony colloid; D. Gold sol
List - II (use): I. Eye lotion; II. Kalaazar; III. Cottrell precipitator; IV. Intramuscular injection
The correct answer is

options.text: A - III, B - I, C - IV, D - II
A - III, B - I, C - II, D - IV
A - IV, B - II, C - I, D - III
A - II, B - I, C - III, D - IV

explanation: Smoke particles are removed by the Cottrell electrostatic precipitator (A-III); colloidal silver (argyrol) is an eye lotion (B-I); colloidal antimony treats kala-azar (C-II); colloidal gold is given by intramuscular injection (D-IV). Option (1) swaps antimony and gold.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q146)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: The ore calamine on calcination gives its oxide X. The common name of X is
explanation: Calamine is $\mathrm{ZnCO_3}$; calcination: $\mathrm{ZnCO_3\to ZnO+CO_2}$. ZnO occurs naturally as zincite. Cuprite is $\mathrm{Cu_2O}$, bauxite is hydrated $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$, siderite is $\mathrm{FeCO_3}$.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q147)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: The reduction products formed when copper and zinc metals are separately oxidised with dilute $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ respectively are
explanation: $\mathrm{3Cu+8HNO_3(dil)\to3Cu(NO_3)_2+2NO+4H_2O}$; $\mathrm{4Zn+10HNO_3(dil)\to4Zn(NO_3)_2+N_2O+5H_2O}$. More electropositive Zn reduces nitrate further. $\mathrm{NO_2}$ forms with concentrated acid.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q148)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: In which of the following, elements are correctly arranged in the increasing order of unpaired electrons?
explanation: Ground states: Mn $3d^54s^2$ (5 unpaired), Fe $3d^6$ (4), Co $3d^7$ (3), Ni $3d^8$ (2). Increasing: Ni < Co < Fe < Mn. Option (3) is the reverse (decreasing) order.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q150)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: The metal ion, ligands present in Wilkinson catalyst are respectively
explanation: Wilkinson's catalyst is $\mathrm{[RhCl(PPh_3)_3]}$: one $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ and three neutral $\mathrm{PPh_3}$, so Rh is +1. Trap: assuming the common +3 state of Rh.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q151)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
Consider the following statements
Statement-I: Polystyrene is a thermosetting polymer
Statement-II: Bakelite is a thermoplastic polymer
The correct answer is

options.text: Both Statement-I and statement-II are correct
Statement-I is correct but statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct but statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and statement-II are not correct

explanation: Polystyrene is a thermoplastic (softens on heating, linear chains), and Bakelite is a thermosetting polymer (cross-linked network). Both statements have the classes swapped, so both are incorrect.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q152)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: The incorrect statement in the following is

options.text: Cellulose is a straight chain polysaccharide of $\alpha$-D-glucose units through $C_1-C_4$ glycosidic linkage
Glycogen is found in Yeast and fungi
Glycogen is also known as animal starch

explanation: Cellulose is made of $\beta$-D-glucose units joined by $\beta$-$C_1-C_4$ glycosidic links; $\alpha$-glucose units form starch. Amylopectin is branched ($C_1-C_4$ chain, $C_1-C_6$ branches); glycogen (animal starch) also occurs in yeast and fungi.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q153)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: Which of the following structures represent an example of a tranquilizer?

options.text: 5,5-diethylbarbituric acid (pyrimidine-2,4,6-trione ring with two $\mathrm{C_2H_5}$ groups at C-5)

explanation: 5,5-Diethylbarbituric acid (veronal) is a barbiturate - a hypnotic/sedative tranquilizer. (2) is histamine (a target of antihistamines/antacids), (3) is sulphanilamide (an antibacterial), and (1) is an amphetamine-type stimulant amine, not a tranquilizer.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q154)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
What are X and Y respectively in the following set of reactions?
$\mathrm{C_6H_5F} \xleftarrow{\;Y\;} \mathrm{C_6H_5N_2Cl} \xrightarrow{\;X\;} \mathrm{C_6H_5Cl}$
explanation: Chlorobenzene from benzenediazonium chloride needs Cu/HCl (Gattermann) or CuCl/HCl (Sandmeyer). Fluorobenzene is made by the Balz-Schiemann reaction: $\mathrm{HBF_4}$ gives $\mathrm{ArN_2^+BF_4^-}$, which on heating gives ArF. HCl, KCl or KF alone do not replace the diazo group.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q155)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
Consider the following reactions I, II and III. The correct order of reactivity of X, Y and Z towards $S_N1$ reaction is
(I) $\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2-CH_3} \xrightarrow{HBr}$ X (major)
(II) $\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2-CH_3} \xrightarrow[(C_6H_5CO)_2O_2]{HBr}$ Y (major)
(III) $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C=CH_2} \xrightarrow{HBr}$ Z
explanation: X = 2-bromobutane (Markovnikov, 2$^\circ$); Y = 1-bromobutane (peroxide/anti-Markovnikov, 1$^\circ$); Z = tert-butyl bromide (3$^\circ$). $S_N1$ rate follows carbocation stability 3$^\circ$ > 2$^\circ$ > 1$^\circ$: Z > X > Y. Trap: forgetting the peroxide effect makes Y = X.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q156)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
Consider the following reaction
Cumene $\xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } H_3O^+]{\text{(i) } O_2}$ A + B
A is acidic in nature and forms salt with aq. NaOH. A and B are converted to corresponding hydrocarbons with reagents X and Y respectively. What are X and Y?
explanation: Cumene hydroperoxide cleavage gives A = phenol (acidic) and B = acetone. Phenol $\to$ benzene by distillation with zinc dust; acetone $\to$ propane by Clemmensen reduction (Zn-Hg/HCl). $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$ only reduces acetone to 2-propanol, not to a hydrocarbon; option (4) swaps the reagents.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q157)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
What are X and Y respectively in the following set of reactions?
$\mathrm{C_6H_5CN} \xrightarrow{X} A$ ; $\mathrm{C_6H_5CN} \xrightarrow{Y} B$ ; $A + B \xrightarrow{H^+} \mathrm{C_6H_5C(CH_3)=N-CH_2C_6H_5}$
explanation: The imine comes from benzylamine (A) + acetophenone (B). $\mathrm{C_6H_5CN}$ + Na/EtOH (Mendius) gives $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2NH_2}$; $\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}$ then $\mathrm{H_2O}$ gives $\mathrm{C_6H_5COCH_3}$. $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2Cd}$ does not convert nitriles to ketones (it reacts with acyl chlorides), and DIBAL-H gives benzaldehyde, not the amine.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q158)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
What are X and Y in the following set of reactions?
Toluene $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) } KMnO_4|OH^-\ \text{(ii) } H_3O^+\ \text{(iii) } Br_2|Fe}$ X
Toluene $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) } Br_2|Fe\ \text{(ii) } KMnO_4|OH^-\ \text{(iii) } H_3O^+}$ Y
explanation: For X, oxidation first gives benzoic acid; $-$COOH is meta-directing, so bromination gives 3-bromobenzoic acid. For Y, bromination first ($\mathrm{CH_3}$ is o/p-directing) gives mainly 4-bromotoluene, which oxidises to 4-bromobenzoic acid. Order of steps decides the regiochemistry.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q159)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
In which of the following set/s, reactant and reagent are correctly matched to get ethyl isonitrile as major product?
I. $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl}$ - AgCN
II. $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}$ - $\mathrm{NH_2OH}$, $\mathrm{(CH_3CO)_2O}$
III. $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2}$ - $\mathrm{CHCl_3/OH^-}$, $\Delta$
The correct answer is
explanation: I: covalent AgCN attacks through N, giving $\mathrm{C_2H_5NC}$. III: carbylamine reaction of a 1$^\circ$ amine gives $\mathrm{C_2H_5NC}$. II: propanal oxime dehydrated by $\mathrm{(CH_3CO)_2O}$ gives the nitrile $\mathrm{C_2H_5CN}$ (ethyl cyanide), not the isonitrile.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q160)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: $\beta = \dfrac{F}{v^2}\cos(\alpha t)$, if $F$ is force, $v$ is velocity, $t$ is time, then the dimensional formulae of $\alpha$, $\beta$ are respectively
explanation: The argument of cosine is dimensionless, so $[\alpha]=[T^{-1}]$. Cosine itself is dimensionless, so $[\beta]=[F]/[v^2]=\dfrac{MLT^{-2}}{L^2T^{-2}}=[ML^{-1}T^0]$. Option (1) wrongly treats $\alpha$ as dimensionless; option (2) mistakes $F/v^2$ for $MLT^0$.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q81)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: Cars X and Y begin the race simultaneously with velocities $8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, moving in a straight line with uniform accelerations $2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ and $4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ respectively. If they reach final point at the same instant, then the length of the path is
explanation: Equal distances in equal time: $8t+t^2=4t+2t^2\Rightarrow t=4$ s. Length $=8(4)+\tfrac12(2)(16)=32+16=48$ m. 32 m is only the uniform-velocity part of X's distance; 16 m is only the acceleration part.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q82)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A projectile is thrown into space so that it attains a maximum possible range of 200 m. Taking the point of projection as origin, the coordinates of the point where the velocity of projectile is minimum is
explanation: Maximum range means $\theta=45^\circ$, $R=u^2/g=200$ m. Speed is minimum at the highest point: $x=R/2=100$ m, $H=u^2/(4g)=R/4=50$ m. So $(100,50)$. Swapping coordinates or using $H=R/2$ gives the wrong options.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q83)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A bike race is conducted on a circular track of radius 60 m. If the slowest bike, weighing 120 kg, moved around the track at a constant speed of 108 kmph, then the time taken by it to complete one lap and its acceleration are respectively
explanation: $v=108$ km/h $=30$ m/s. $T=2\pi r/v=2\pi(60)/30\approx12.56$ s. Centripetal acceleration $a=v^2/r=900/60=15\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Constant speed does not mean zero acceleration (trap in option 3); mass is irrelevant.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q84)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A block is kept at the top of a rough inclined plane of length 2.8 m and angle of inclination $\cos^{-1}(0.6)$. If the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the upper half of the plane is 0.3 and between the block and the lower half of the plane is 0.5, then the velocity with which the block reaches the bottom of the plane is (acceleration due to gravity $=10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$)
explanation: $\cos\theta=0.6,\ \sin\theta=0.8$. Upper half (1.4 m): $a_1=10(0.8-0.3\times0.6)=6.2$; lower half: $a_2=10(0.8-0.5\times0.6)=5$. $v^2=2(6.2)(1.4)+2(5)(1.4)=17.36+14=31.36$, so $v=5.6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Using a single $\mu$ for the whole plane gives wrong values.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q85)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A stone of mass 400 g tied to one end of a string is rotated in a horizontal circle of radius 125 m. If the string can withstand a maximum tension of $50\pi^2$ N, then the minimum time period with which the stone can be rotated is
explanation: Tension $=m\omega^2r=m\dfrac{4\pi^2}{T^2}r=\dfrac{0.4\times4\pi^2\times125}{T^2}=\dfrac{200\pi^2}{T^2}\le50\pi^2\Rightarrow T^2\ge4$, so $T_{\min}=2$ s. Smaller period means larger tension, so the minimum period corresponds to maximum tension.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q86)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A body of mass 5 kg is projected vertically upwards from a point X from the ground with an initial speed of $20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. It rises to a point Y where its kinetic energy is reduced to 400 J. If the body experiences a constant air resistance of 10 N throughout its motion, then the vertical distance between X and Y is (Acceleration due to gravity $=10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$)
explanation: Initial KE $=\tfrac12(5)(400)=1000$ J. Loss $=600$ J $=(mg+f)h=(50+10)h\Rightarrow h=10$ m. Ignoring air resistance gives $600/50=12$ m (not listed); using $mg-f$ gives 15 m.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q87)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: Three balls A, B and C of equal mass are moving in the same order along the same straight line on a smooth horizontal surface. Initially, ball A moves towards right with a velocity of $6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, ball B moves towards left with a velocity of $4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and ball C moves towards right with a velocity of $3\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. If the coefficient of restitution between any two balls is 0.8, then the relative velocity of balls B and C after collision is
explanation: A–B (equal masses): $v=\frac{u_1+u_2}{2}\mp\frac{e(u_1-u_2)}{2}$ with $6,-4$: $v_A=1-4=-3$, $v_B=1+4=5$. B–C with $5,3$: $v_B=4-0.8=3.2$, $v_C=4+0.8=4.8$. Relative velocity $=4.8-3.2=1.6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ $(=e\times2)$. A moves left, so no further collision.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q88)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: If three particles of masses $2m$, $m$ and $4m$ are moving in three mutually perpendicular directions with velocities $3\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $3\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ respectively, then the magnitude of the velocity of the center of mass of the system of three particles is
explanation: Momenta: $6m, 4m, 12m$ along perpendicular axes. $|\vec p|=m\sqrt{36+16+144}=14m$. $v_{cm}=14m/7m=2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Adding magnitudes as scalars ($22m/7m\approx3.1$) is the common trap.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q89)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: The acceleration of a uniform disc rolling down an inclined plane of length 1.75 m is 1/3 times the acceleration due to gravity. If a solid sphere is rolling down from the top of the same inclined plane, then the velocity with which it reaches the bottom of the plane is
explanation: Disc: $a=\tfrac23g\sin\theta=g/3\Rightarrow\sin\theta=\tfrac12$. Sphere: $a=\tfrac57g\sin\theta=\tfrac{5g}{14}$. $v^2=2aL=2\cdot\tfrac{5g}{14}\cdot1.75=1.25g=12.25$ (with $g=9.8$), so $v=3.5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Using the disc's acceleration for the sphere gives a smaller value.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q90)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: In simple harmonic motion, at mean position
explanation: At the mean position displacement is zero, so speed (hence KE) is maximum, while PE $=\tfrac12kx^2$ and acceleration $=-\omega^2x$ are both zero. PE maximum, KE zero and maximum acceleration all occur at the extreme positions.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q91)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A particle starting from the origin executes simple harmonic motion along $x$-axis. Its velocity at any instant $t$ is given by $v_x=22\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{2}\right)\ \mathrm{cm\,s^{-1}}$. The total distance covered by the particle in time $t=4.5$ sec
explanation: $x=\dfrac{44}{\pi}\sin\dfrac{\pi t}{2}$, so $A=44/\pi\approx14.0$ cm and $T=4$ s. In 4 s distance $=4A$; in the next 0.5 s it goes from 0 to $A\sin(\pi/4)=0.707A$. Total $=4.707A\approx65.9$ cm. Using displacement instead of distance, or $4.5/4\times4A$, gives wrong answers.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q92)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A 1200 kg artificial satellite is in an orbit of radius $2R_E$ about the earth. The energy required to transfer it to an orbit of radius $3R_E$ is ($g=10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, $R_E=6400$ km)
explanation: Orbital energy $E=-\dfrac{GMm}{2r}$. $\Delta E=\dfrac{GMm}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2R}-\dfrac{1}{3R}\right)=\dfrac{GMm}{12R}=\dfrac{mgR}{12}=\dfrac{1200\times10\times6.4\times10^6}{12}=6.4\times10^9$ J. Using only the PE difference (forgetting KE change) doubles the answer.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q93)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A copper wire of negligible mass, length 1 m and area of cross-section $10^{-6}\ \mathrm{m^2}$ is kept on a smooth horizontal table. One end of the wire is fixed and other end of the wire attached with a ball of mass 1 kg. If the ball and wire are rotating with $20\ \mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$, an elongation of $10^{-3}$ m is observed in the wire, find its Young's modulus
explanation: Tension $=m\omega^2r=1\times400\times1=400$ N. $Y=\dfrac{FL}{A\,\Delta L}=\dfrac{400\times1}{10^{-6}\times10^{-3}}=4\times10^{11}\ \mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}$. Option (4) is just the tension; option (3) forgets the elongation factor.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q94)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: Calculate the amount of work done in spraying a drop of a liquid of radius 1 mm into million identical droplets under isothermal conditions. [surface tension of liquid $=550\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{N\,m^{-1}}$]
explanation: $n=10^6\Rightarrow r=R/n^{1/3}=R/100$. $W=T\,\Delta A=4\pi R^2T(n^{1/3}-1)=4\pi(10^{-6})(0.55)(99)\approx6.84\times10^{-4}$ J. Option (4) is half this value; using $n^{1/3}$ instead of $n^{1/3}-1$ gives about $6.9\times10^{-4}$ J.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q95)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A blackened platinum wire of surface area $10^{-5}\ \mathrm{m^2}$ is maintained at temperature of 3000 K. At what rate the wire is loosing energy [Stefan–Boltzman constant $\sigma=5.67\times10^{-8}\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}K^{-4}}$]
explanation: $P=\sigma AT^4=5.67\times10^{-8}\times10^{-5}\times(3000)^4=5.67\times10^{-13}\times8.1\times10^{13}\approx45.9\approx46$ W. Errors in evaluating $T^4=81\times10^{12}$ lead to the other options.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q96)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: An earthen pitcher containing 9.5 kg of water loses one gram of water per minute due to evaporation. If water equivalent of pitcher is 0.5 kg. The time required to cool the water in pitcher from 30°C to 28°C is (Neglect radiation effect and Take latent heat of vaporization $500\ \mathrm{cal\,g^{-1}}$)
explanation: Heat to be removed $=(9500+500)\times1\times2=20000$ cal. Evaporation removes $1\times500=500$ cal/min. Time $=20000/500=40$ min. Forgetting the pitcher's water equivalent gives 38 min; forgetting the 2°C factor gives 20 min.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q97)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A Carnot engine of 50% efficiency takes heat from a source of 400 K. To change efficiency to 70% without changing the sink temperature, the new temperature of source should be (nearer to)
explanation: $0.5=1-T_2/400\Rightarrow T_2=200$ K. New: $0.7=1-200/T_1'\Rightarrow T_1'=200/0.3\approx667$ K. Scaling the source temperature linearly with efficiency ($400\times0.7/0.5=560$ K) is the common mistake.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q98)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: In which of the following thermodynamic process, the internal energy of system remains constant
explanation: For an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature, so it stays constant when $T$ is constant (isothermal). In isobaric and isochoric processes $T$ generally changes; in adiabatic processes $\Delta U=-W\neq0$.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q99)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: The rms speed of oxygen molecule at some temperature is $150\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Then the rms speed of hydrogen molecule at the same temperature is
explanation: $v_{rms}\propto1/\sqrt{M}$: $v_{H_2}=150\sqrt{32/2}=150\times4=600\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Using the mass ratio without the square root would give 2400; inverting the ratio gives a smaller speed.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q100)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: Two identical strings $A$ and $B$ of same material are having tensions $T_A$ and $T_B$ respectively. If their fundamental frequencies are 450 Hz and 300 Hz, then $T_A/T_B$ is
explanation: $f=\dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{T/\mu}$ with same $L,\mu$, so $T\propto f^2$: $T_A/T_B=(450/300)^2=9/4$. Option (3) uses the frequency ratio directly; option (1) inverts it.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q101)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: The refractive index of water is $\dfrac{4}{3}$ and that of glass is $\dfrac{3}{2}$. The refractive index of glass with respect to water is
explanation: ${}_w\mu_g=\mu_g/\mu_w=\dfrac{3/2}{4/3}=\dfrac98$. Option (2) is the refractive index of water with respect to glass (inverted ratio).

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q102)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: For the same angle of incidence, the angles of refraction of light ray in different media $A, B, C$ are $35^\circ, 25^\circ, 15^\circ$. If $V_A, V_B, V_C$ are velocities of light in $A, B, C$ media respectively, then
explanation: By Snell's law $\mu=\sin i/\sin r$: smaller $r$ means larger $\mu$, so $\mu_A<\mu_B<\mu_C$. Since $v=c/\mu$, $V_A>V_B>V_C$. Option (4) wrongly associates more bending with higher speed.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q103)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: In a Young's double slit experiment, the intensity at a point where the path difference is $\dfrac{\lambda}{6}$ ($\lambda$ being the wavelength of the light used) is $I$. If $I_0$ denotes the maximum intensity, $\dfrac{I}{I_0}$ is
explanation: Phase difference $\phi=\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\cdot\dfrac{\lambda}{6}=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. $I=I_0\cos^2(\phi/2)=I_0\cos^2 30^\circ=\tfrac34I_0$. Option (2) forgets to square the cosine; option (3) uses $\cos^2 60^\circ$ (not halving $\phi$).

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q104)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: Two identical balls each of mass $\dfrac{40}{3}$ g carry equal and opposite charge. They are suspended from a horizontal plate by silk threads each of length 1 m with a separation of 1.5 m between points of suspension. At equilibrium, if the distance between the balls is 30 cm then, magnitude of charge on each ball is (Acceleration due to gravity $=10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$)
explanation: Opposite charges attract, so each ball moves inward by $(1.5-0.3)/2=0.6$ m: $\sin\theta=0.6$, $\tan\theta=0.75$. $F=mg\tan\theta=\tfrac{40}{3}\times10^{-3}\times10\times0.75=0.1$ N. $q^2=\dfrac{Fr^2}{k}=\dfrac{0.1\times0.09}{9\times10^9}=10^{-12}\Rightarrow q=10^{-6}$ C.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q105)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A conducting sphere of radius 4 cm is charged such that it has a potential of 5 V on its surface. Then the potential at a point which is at a depth of 1 cm from its surface is
explanation: Inside a conductor $E=0$, so the potential is the same everywhere inside as on the surface: 5 V. Scaling with distance (e.g. $5\times3/4$) wrongly applies the outside formula or treats it as a non-conducting sphere.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q106)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A potentiometer wire is 10 m long and has a resistance of $18\ \Omega$. It is connected to a battery of emf 5 V and internal resistance $2\ \Omega$. Calculate the potential gradient along the wire.
explanation: $I=5/(18+2)=0.25$ A. Potential across the wire $=0.25\times18=4.5$ V, so gradient $=4.5/10=0.45\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$. Ignoring internal resistance gives 0.5; option (4) confuses the current with the gradient.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q109)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A proton and a deuteron, both having the same kinetic energy, enter perpendicularly into a uniform magnetic field B. For motion of proton and deuteron on circular path of radius $R_p$ and $R_d$ respectively, the correct statement is
explanation: $R=\dfrac{mv}{qB}=\dfrac{\sqrt{2mK}}{qB}$. Same $K$ and $q$, deuteron mass $=2m_p$, so $R_d=\sqrt2R_p$. $R_d=2R_p$ would hold for equal speeds, and $R_d=R_p$ for equal momenta.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q110)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A wire carrying current I and other parallel wire carrying current 2I in the same direction produces a magnetic field B at the midpoint between them. Then the magnitude of field at the same point, when the 2I wire is switched off
explanation: At the midpoint (distance $d$ from each), fields of like-directed currents oppose: $B=\dfrac{\mu_0}{2\pi d}(2I-I)=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi d}$. With the 2I wire off, field $=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi d}=B$. Adding the fields ($3I$) instead of subtracting leads to the wrong options.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q111)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: The earth's magnetic field at a certain place has a total strength of 0.5 Gauss and the horizontal component of 0.3 Gauss. Then the angle of dip at that place is
explanation: $\cos\delta=B_H/B=0.3/0.5=3/5$, so $B_V=0.4$ G and $\tan\delta=B_V/B_H=4/3$. Option (1) inverts the ratio; option (4) uses $\sin\delta=3/5$, confusing horizontal with vertical component.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q112)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: A 2 m long solenoid with diameter 2 cm and 2000 turns has a secondary coil of 1000 turns wound closely near its midpoint. The mutual inductance between the two coils is
explanation: $M=\dfrac{\mu_0N_1N_2A}{L}=\dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times2000\times1000\times\pi(0.01)^2}{2}\approx3.95\times10^{-4}$ H. Using the diameter instead of the radius in the area gives four times this value.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q113)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem:
In the given circuit, the readings of voltmeters $V_1$ and $V_2$ are 300 V each. The reading of voltmeter $V_3$ and ammeter A are respectively
[Circuit: an inductor L, a capacitor C and a resistor $R=100\ \Omega$ in series with an ammeter A across a 220 V, 50 Hz AC source; voltmeters $V_1$, $V_2$, $V_3$ are connected across L, C and R respectively.]
explanation: $V_L=V_C=300$ V means resonance: $V=\sqrt{V_R^2+(V_L-V_C)^2}=V_R=220$ V. Current $I=V_R/R=220/100=2.2$ A. Assuming $V_R$ must be less than the source voltage, or that $V_L, V_C$ cannot exceed 220 V, is the trap.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q114)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: Electromagnetic waves do not transport
explanation: EM waves are oscillating electric and magnetic fields; they carry energy, momentum (radiation pressure) and information, but they are electrically neutral and carry no charge.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q115)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: Work function of a metallic surface is 5.01 eV. When a light of wavelength 2000 Å falls on the metallic surface, it emits photo electrons. The potential difference required to stop the fastest photo electron is? (in Volt)
explanation: $E=\dfrac{12400}{2000}\ \text{eV}=6.2$ eV. $eV_0=E-\phi=6.2-5.01=1.19\approx1.2$ V. Errors in the value of $hc$ or in the unit conversion shift the answer to the distractors.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q116)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: The atomic number (Z) of a hydrogen like atom whose shortest wavelength of Brackett Series is same as the shortest wavelength of Balmer series of hydrogen atom is
explanation: Shortest wavelength (series limit): Brackett $\dfrac1\lambda=\dfrac{RZ^2}{16}$, Balmer of H $\dfrac1\lambda=\dfrac{R}{4}$. Equating, $Z^2=4\Rightarrow Z=2$. Using $Z$ instead of $Z^2$ gives $Z=4$.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q117)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: Binding energy per nucleon of deuteron and Helium nuclei are 1.1 MeV and 7 MeV respectively. If a single Helium nucleus was formed by adding two Deuterons, the energy released is
explanation: BE of He $=4\times7=28$ MeV; BE of two deuterons $=2\times(2\times1.1)=4.4$ MeV. Energy released $=28-4.4=23.6$ MeV. Forgetting to multiply by the nucleon number gives wrong values.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q118)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: The minimum energy gap of a semi-conductor used in manufacturing LED is
explanation: (The Telugu version specifies LEDs emitting visible light.) Visible light spans about 1.8 eV (red, ~700 nm) to 3 eV (violet). So the minimum band gap needed is about 1.8 eV. Larger values like 3 eV correspond to the violet end, not the minimum.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q119)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: physics
stem: If $f_m$ is a modulating frequency and $f_c$ is carrier wave frequency, then Bandwidth in Amplitude Modulated wave is
explanation: An AM wave contains $f_c$ and side bands $f_c\pm f_m$. Bandwidth $=(f_c+f_m)-(f_c-f_m)=2f_m$. $f_c+f_m$ is only the upper side band frequency.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 1, Q120)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: Consider the elements with atomic number ($Z$) from 11 to 18. The ratio of number of $s$-electrons to $p$-electrons in element $X$ is $2:3$ and in element $Y$ is $3:5$. What are $X$ and $Y$?
explanation: From Mg onward the $s$-electron count is fixed at 6 ($1s^2 2s^2 3s^2$). P: $p = 6+3 = 9$, so $6:9 = 2:3$. S: $p = 6+4 = 10$, so $6:10 = 3:5$. Hence $X$ = P and $Y$ = S. For comparison, Si gives $6:8 = 3:4$ and Cl gives $6:11$, which is why the neighbouring pairs fail.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 2, Q122)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: Which of the following statements is not correct regarding third period elements?

options.text: $\mathrm{Cl}$ has the highest electron gain enthalpy
$\mathrm{Ar}$ has the highest first ionization enthalpy
Mg has higher ionization enthalpy than $\mathrm{Al}$
P has a lower first ionization enthalpy than $\mathrm{S}$

explanation: P has a half-filled $3p^3$ configuration, which is extra stable, so its first IE (1012 kJ/mol) is higher than that of S (1000 kJ/mol). Statement (4) is therefore false. The other statements are true: Cl has the most negative electron gain enthalpy, Ar has the highest IE in the period, and Mg ($3s^2$) has a higher IE than Al, whose $3p^1$ electron is easier to remove.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 2, Q123)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: Which one of the following orders is not correctly matched with the property mentioned against it?
explanation: Dipole moments: $\mathrm{NF_3}$ (0.23 D) < $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ (1.04 D) < $\mathrm{NH_3}$ (1.47 D). In $\mathrm{NF_3}$ the lone-pair moment opposes the bond moments, so $\mathrm{NF_3}$ belongs below $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ and order (3) is wrong. The other orders are correct: BDE 431 < 498 < 945 kJ/mol; bond angles 104.5° < 117° < 119°; covalent character rises as the cation gets smaller (Fajans' rules).

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 2, Q124)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.text: $\mathrm{CO, N_2, O_2^{2+}}$ have same bond order
The bond between third element of 1st group and second element of 17th group is ionic in nature
The total number of $sp^2$ hybrid orbitals in benzene is 12

explanation: Each of the 6 carbons in benzene forms 3 $sp^2$ hybrid orbitals, giving $6\times3 = 18$, not 12. A common trap is to count only the 12 σ bonds. The other statements are true: CO, $\mathrm{N_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_2^{2+}}$ are isoelectronic (14 e⁻) with bond order 3; K–Cl (KCl) is ionic; $o$-nitrophenol is chelated through intramolecular H-bonding.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 2, Q125)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: At T(K), the kinetic energy of one mole of an ideal gas (molar mass = $M\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$) is $Y\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$. What is its most probable velocity ($U_{mp}$) in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$?
explanation: $\tfrac32RT = 1000Y$ J gives $RT = \tfrac{2000Y}{3}$. Then $U_{mp} = \sqrt{\tfrac{2RT}{M\times10^{-3}}} = \sqrt{\tfrac{4\times10^6Y}{3M}} = 2\times10^3\sqrt{\tfrac{Y}{3M}}$. Option (2) drops the factor of 2 by treating $U_{mp}$ as $\sqrt{RT/M}$. Options (1) and (3) invert the ratio.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 2, Q126)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem:
Consider the unbalanced equation given below
$a\,\mathrm{Cr(OH)_3} + b\,\mathrm{IO_3^-} + c\,\mathrm{OH^-} \rightarrow d\,\mathrm{CrO_4^{2-}} + e\,\mathrm{I^-} + f\,\mathrm{H_2O}$
Identify the correct statements/equations given below
I. $\mathrm{Cr(OH)_3}$ is reduced to $\mathrm{CrO_4^{2-}}$
II. $a+b+c=7$
III. $a+c=d+f$
IV. $\mathrm{IO_3^-}$ acts as an oxidizing agent in this reaction
The correct answer is
explanation: Cr goes from +3 to +6 (loses 3e⁻) and I from +5 to −1 (gains 6e⁻). Balanced: $2\mathrm{Cr(OH)_3} + \mathrm{IO_3^-} + 4\mathrm{OH^-} \to 2\mathrm{CrO_4^{2-}} + \mathrm{I^-} + 5\mathrm{H_2O}$. So $a+b+c = 7$ (II true). $a+c = 6 \ne d+f = 7$ (III false). Cr is oxidised, not reduced (I false). $\mathrm{IO_3^-}$ is the oxidant (IV true).

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 2, Q127)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: At 27°C, 10 g of argon (at. wt = 40 u) is compressed isothermally and reversibly from 50 L to 5 L. What is $q$ for this process? (Assume Ar as an ideal gas) ($R = 8.3\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}mol^{-1}}$)
explanation: $n = 0.25$ mol. Work done on the gas: $w = nRT\ln(V_1/V_2) = 0.25\times8.3\times300\times2.303 = +1433$ J. For an ideal gas held isothermal, $\Delta U = 0$, so $q = -w = -1.433$ kJ (heat is released on compression). Option (1) gets the sign wrong. Options (3) and (4) use $n = 0.5$.

source.name: AP EAPCET 2026 (official master paper with preliminary key, 13 May Shift 2, Q128)
source.licence: Official exam-authority release; for personal practice

subject: chemistry
stem: At 298 K for the reaction, $\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)}$, enthalpy and entropy changes are $-92.4\ \mathrm{kJ}$ and $-200\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ respectively. The value of $\log K_c$ for the reaction is ($R = 8.3\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}mol^{-1}}$)
explanation: $\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H - T\Delta S = -92400 + 298\times200 = -32800$ J. $\log K = \dfrac{-\Delta G^\circ}{2.303RT} = \dfrac{32800}{2.303\times8.3\times298} \approx 5.75$. A frequent mistake is to forget converting $\Delta S$ from J to kJ, or to use $\ln$ in place of $\log$.
